chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, saying: Muhammad ibn Nasir told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa told us, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about tafath, so he said: It is shaving and what is in the skin of a person.

key_terms.التَّفَث: Tafath: Shaving hair or removing what is in the skin that breaks ritual purity.
key_terms.جِلْدُ الْإِنْسَانِ: Jild al-insan: The skin of a person.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of tafath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'tafath' refers specifically to shaving hair and removing obstructions from the skin, such as dirt or nail clippings, which must be cleared for the validity of prayer. This definition highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on physical cleanliness (*taharah*) as a prerequisite for ritual acts, distinguishing it from mere washing. The chain of transmission underscores the reliability of the *Ahl al-Bayt*’s direct explanations of ritual terminology.
